utterances.text: Is that the meeting where you referred to Mr. Karadzic speaking about the Muslims to be driven into the valleys, or which -- can you give us a hint which meeting?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the meeting at which Karadzic said words to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I think that should be enough for this intercept. The next intercept, I do not think we need to play. It's tab 22, and I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next is tab 22, and I have marked a passage for the witness, and also a passage to be put on the ELMO. It is tab 22. It's on the first page. And there is a passage in there --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, did you listen to a conversation between Radovan Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic where they speak about Wijnaendts' visit, a visit?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have to go into private session. I just see that it cannot be discussed in the open. 9 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you look at the text in front of you, it says here Slobodan Milosevic says: "Listen. This Wijnaendts will visit that Milan today." Is that referring to you? Did you expect to meet Mr. Wijnaendts?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That was Wijnaendts' second visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now I will quote Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, and he says: "And he told me yesterday that when he had been in that place over there, they had shown him that the effects had been particularly disastrous where they had been attacked by some Serbs, and so on. He saw big craters. I don't know ... from these shells, and so on. I don't believe they showed him everything that those Martic's forces had done, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. but probably that they themselves had done and then made it seem as if it were that." Sir, in the beginning of this transcript, we see the name Gospic mentioned. What had happened in Gospic that was shown to Mr. Wijnaendts and Mr. Milosevic is referring to?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting around Gospic between Serbian forces, which were attacking Gospic, intending to gain control over eastern Gospic, and forces of the Croatian government that were defending Gospic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had Martic's forces done disastrous things?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What? Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mortar fire was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Against civilian targets or just against the army?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have precise insight into what was happening on the ground, but as a rule, targets -- were targeted non-selectively.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I would like to go now further in this intercept and to the next marked page. Your Honour, it's on page 3, on the -- actually, on top of the page, and I would like to quote: SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: That, probably, wasn't done by Serbs, but by this lot. So, he should absolutely, independently of that conversation of theirs for which he should, implying that he doesn't know of it, point out the consequences in Gospic. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right. I'll ring him now. I think that he's not enough ... he is a bit inflexible. He is not enough, er, enough flexible and wise to do so. Yes, he ... he has that minor flaw and he doesn't understand that you have to play the game when they set things up in that way. This lot are great masters of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can't find this passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's on page 3, and it's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's page 2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I have a slightly older version of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we have it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. It's on the ELMO also now, in the middle, actually. Yes. Stop. Stop. It's right there. And I was reading -- and now it's Mr. Milosevic: "That's why I'm telling you. It should be counterbalanced in a way, that ... his impression now that that lot did something in Gospic, caused great destruction, and so on. He should also tell him, they did this and that over there." I have to go for one question into private session related to this sector. 18 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually -- did Mr. Karadzic actually call you and instruct you or had a conversation of what to say to Mr. Wijnaendts?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to somebody. I'm not quite sure that it was Karadzic, but yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you told to do when you met Mr. Wijnaendts?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To show him what the Croats had done to the Serbs around Knin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that understood to be counterbalancing what the Serbs had done in Gospic?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, to establish some kind of a balanced picture of reciprocal destruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that something that was usually done to stress the violence of the other side to make it look better what their own side did? Was that a typical behaviour during international negotiations or meetings?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was typical. One would highlight the effects of the other side, exaggerate what they had done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, going now a little bit further down in the text, there is a reference of -- or rather, a question that Mr. Radovan Karadzic has in relation to Kostajnica, and he asks Mr. Milosevic: "Yes, yes. All right. Tell me, has Kostajnica been taken, I heard, hasn't it?" And the answer is: "Well, I don't have precise information." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can go into open session. I forgot.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Milosevic -- Mr. Karadzic asked what -- in reference to Kostajnica, what had happened in Kostajnica at that point in time? And we are talking about September 1991.

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting between the forces of the Yugoslav People's Army and the Serbian forces that were endeavouring to capture Kostajnica, that was being held by the forces of the government of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a little bit further down in the text, Mr. Karadzic asks: RADOVAN KARADZIC: Okucani hasn't been taken, has it?" And Mr. Milosevic answers: SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: The results were good up there. Very good results up there, very good. We'll talk later, we can't now over the phone. There were all kinds of things there. RADOVAN KARADZIC: I'm afraid that, that ... the army has retreated over there, and I'm afraid that they'll fail to keep Okucani. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Well, I'll see what the situation is like. RADOVAN KARADZIC: It mustn't happen. I think that Joca has assessed it properly. That's the spine! That's the spine! When you control that, you control the road to Pakrac and everything. What had happened at that time, if anything, in Okucani?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting around Okucani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Joca mentioned here, who is that? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a nickname he was referred to?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a name of endearment for close associates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to go down now to actually the last page. That's page 5 in the English, and I assume it's also in the Serbian, the last page. And there is another reference to Jovica, and it says here Radovan Karadzic says: "Okay, if you can. This Aca was brilliant in all of this, but it's necessary now just to -- I think that Jovica has assessed it wonderfully. We mustn't ... because then they can bargain more easily and in a different way. We must hold that road to Pakrac and all of that." First of all, who is Aca who was brilliant?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aca Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? What did he do in relation to Okucani?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but he was the head of military security. He was mentioned also in the events surrounding Martic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here this reference to Jovica?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are two men who had information about combat activities. They were heads of services that were involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the importance of the road to Pakrac, if anything? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was important for the Serbs because it linked the territory of Western Slavonia with Serb territories in Bosnia and Yugoslavia, or Serbia, rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can now turn to the next intercept, and it's tab 22. And I also do not intend --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We just dealt with 22.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. 21. 21. Tab 21. And I again do not intend to have it played but just discuss one section with the witness. And the section I would like to discuss is on page 10, starting on page 10, the last line, and it's going over into page 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, did you -- looking at this transcript, did you have -- did you listen in to a conversation between Slobodan Milosevic and Radovan Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on the 9th of August, 1991? And I quote now from page 10: SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: No one fights on the borders of Croatia. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: To the contrary... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Inside. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: There, inside Croatia, on the edges of the Serbian territories. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. Are ... are ... the positions such that this would be suitable if it was done, right? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: I think they almost are. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Almost? A little bit up there, Petrinja and Sisak? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Almost like there, there is no, nothing else, no ... any greater difference. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. They should put it naturally, the sooner the better. If Europe is in a hurry to finish the things, there you go. Let them finish the things. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yes, yes. So, let us start slowly, brother, working, and later on we go for a summer holiday, right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at what time was this conversation made, and what was ongoing at that time on the international level? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of August 1991, the European Community had initiated negotiations on a political settlement for Yugoslavia. So this was a follow-up of the activities of the European Community of July 1991. It was a follow-up to those activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is this reference to fighting inside, on the edges of the Serbian territories, and there's also the remark -- the question of Radovan Karadzic in relation to Petrinja and Sisak. What was happening there at that time?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting around Petrinja and Sisak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between whom?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the one side, the JNA garrison from Petrinja and Serb volunteer units; and on the other, the forces of the government of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We are now going to tab 39, and that's actually an intercept that will be played partly. And in relation to -- oh, sorry. Sorry. I think we have already played this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, we haven't. Sorry. 39. And we will play -- in the English translation it will be page 3, starting right in the middle, with the name "Zulfikar was there..." And we will play it until page 5, the first -- the fourth line from the top, ending with: "Yes, yes. Fine. He is here in 'Intercontinental.'" That's the part that we are going to play. And for the technical booth, it's track 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Zulfikar was here, he said he would put it on Television Sarajevo, if they would want to broadcast his show, this Kadic was stating that volunteers from Bosnia were raping the Muslim women, setting the houses on fire, et cetera, they said all that on TV, and he said they wanted to start a war in BiH. RADOVAN KARADZIC: It is over, he started the war, here, I have them here, in front of me, the faxes that Doko sent, by his authorisation, they are transferring all the conscripts that had not been deployed to the reserve forces of the police, actually, who would know if they were deployed or not, since they did not give the records to the army. They are, they are making, today, on 23 September, they started making a state army. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yes, yes. RADOVAN KARADZIC: And I informed the Main Staff about it, Acic was not there, but I told it to the duty officer, we now have to, I don't know whether to advise our people to respond or not to respond. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: To respond, by all means, by all means, because they will clash with the army. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: And then you will have the army on one side and those on others on the other. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Respond, by all means, as there is nobody but the army. RADOVAN KARADZIC: No, no. To respond to the police reserve forces, that is what I'm asking you. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Who? Ours? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: No way, brother. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Well, no, but if they respond, they will get the weapons, to, and they will not be able to... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: I know, but they have to respond to the army and, and... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Fine. They're responding to the army. The response here is not that bad. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Well, I know, but look what they're doing. There are all kinds of instigators here, and did you see what Martic said yesterday, here, for Draskovic? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. I saw, he let us know. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: It should also come from people, similarly. Here, SPS? He did say something, not about Draskovic, but about this... RADOVAN KARADZIC: We had it the other day also. I read it to you. I see they corrected it slightly in politics, but fine. It is... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Fine. But, do it again today, this regarding ... in the line of what Martic said, and to absolutely support the army. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Right. Did you ... did you see what Biljana and Nikola did? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: I haven't seen it yet. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Well, it was sent to Mira. Please, let them, let them... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: It has been up to now, BBC was, then ... this Adil came by to say, to say a few words... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Can Aco do that for him, no? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Well, I hope he can. Here, we will see now. Is this dossier related to him? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. To him there. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: To Aliju? RADOVAN KARADZIC: No, not to Sabic. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: To Sabic. Yes. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yes, yes. I hope it is possible, I... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Let them, let the two of them make ... let Aco immediately make contact with him directly. It will be for the best. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yes, yes, fine. He is here in the "Intercontinental." Then we will see.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, which -- do you recognise the voices?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Slobodan Milosevic and Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say when -- from the contents of this conversation, can you say when it took place?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took place when the mobilisation was stepped up in Serbia, when the opposition protested and when Vuk Draskovic was criticised, saying that he was opposed to the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that? When did that take place?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a reference made to Martic, that he actually -- what -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that he said something about Draskovic. Do you recall whether Martic at that time made speeches against Vuk Draskovic?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did make statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but generally speaking, he criticised him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Karadzic speak about mobilisation of Bosnian forces. Are you aware that at that time also mobilisation took place in Bosnia in September 1991? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, for the area of Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What do you know?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That people were mobilised into the Banja Luka Corps of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is it important to -- that the people get mobilised into the army and not the reserve police? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army was under the authority of Belgrade, or rather, Slobodan Milosevic, and the Yugoslav state presidency, and the police force was under the authority in Bosnia-Herzegovina of Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is also mentioning again of Aco, twice, actually. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aco Vasiljevic. That's the only Aco I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little bit further down from the text that we actually heard, there is a mentioning on that same page, actually, there is mentioned Dubica. Mr. Karadzic says -- it's on page 5, Your Honours, on the second-last line: "Yes, yes. I instructed them in Krajina to see that. It is something in Dubica, some partisan follies. They are now fiddling about the five pointed star about foolish things that Dubica was a partisan town now it will not be partisan." What Dubica is he talking about?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That finishes this tab, and now we go to tab 31, and it is also a conversation that we have to play.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for your orientation, we play from page 2, bottom line, when actually two people are starting to speak while others were ahead of that, and we play it until the very end. And for the technical booth, it's track 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] RADOVAN KARADZIC: Hello. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Radovan. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: I spoke to the highest place. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Right. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Please, you need to understand this, because as they, I don't have ... I cannot explain everything. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: It's of strategic importance for the future RAM, you know what RAM is? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, I know, I know everything. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: That the Banja Luka group is ready and mobile. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: There is why you must first make sure that it is able and mobile and that it has no problems. And secondly, all in one hour call Uzelac and invite him to an agreement at the highest level. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: All the additional people that you can provide. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: That they need to stay and keep their houses and the territory and block those centres of the HDZ, et cetera. They should be armed. They should be provided with everything. We shall fly the helicopters in and all that ... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Excellent. I also ask you to... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Accordingly, I ask you to personally regulate one and two. And this other matter, Kupres, is very important. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Right. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: And the third I told you, the rally, it is very important because of the international community. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, that's under way. But tell me, can we arrange the same thing, that they give me back the armament of the TO in Sipovo and Mrkonjic. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: That's a small matter. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right. Let them arm them there. Here I ... we've got 170 ready in Mrkonjic and 150 in Sipovo and they are ready to go to Kupres. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Is Uzelac also in charge of that? RADOVAN KARADZIC: No, no, this, er, I think that it is him himself yes, yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Tell him that, brother, no problems. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: We cannot discuss every small detail. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right, all right these 150 and 170 shall go to Kupres, and there we've got 750 people... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yes. It is also important for us that this battalion, which was mobilised by the army, is in Kupres and that everything be as it should be. RADOVAN KARADZIC: It will be, but if they receive this. Those who stay under their command, because Kupres is terribly ... that's 50-50 and the Serbs suffered horribly there during the war. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Let me tell you something. Even this crazy Seselj fucked the opposition yesterday. RADOVAN KARADZIC: I saw. I heard. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: You know what he told them? He said, "Did you decide to attack the JNA now when the JNA needs to defend the Serb people?" RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes that's... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: That says the one with the tie of a Zimmerman's waiter. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Fucking hell. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: It's even clear to him... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Clear, clear, certainly. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: And it's not clear to these traitors. RADOVAN KARADZIC: I saw it, I saw. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yesterday in direct contact with Mesic. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Have you got a number for Uzelac by any chance? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: I don't but you shall find it. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Let them find it for you. And please tell him that I wish to secure a maximum political support... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Is he going to accept more of our boys if he needs them or just the ones that already... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: He will receive them if needed. But you give him as many as you judge necessary should stay there. Everything shall be transported for them in the helicopters so they've got everything, so that they stay and guard. RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right, agreed. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Accordingly you've got everything. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Agreed. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: But now it is to be or not to be concerning Krajina because they wish to cut off Krajina. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: They don't want to go to Knin because many would get killed, but they do want to come from behind. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes now we shall... SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: ...in the JNA, that shan't stop them there. How is it going to stop them with the armour alone if there is no brigade? RADOVAN KARADZIC: All right, agreed. Everything will be all right. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: What I mean now is, as they say, war and this is one of the sides. RADOVAN KARADZIC: There are no problems whatsoever. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Please take care of it. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Only if the numbers work, I think it shall be completed. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: You've got everything? Everything must work. RADOVAN KARADZIC: I will, I will. All right. Talk to you, do call again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you recognise the voices of the two persons speaking?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Slobodan Milosevic and Radovan Karadzic were the people having a conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they are speaking about a person, Uzelac. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Nikola Uzelac, Commander of the Banja Luka Corps. Nikola Uzelac, the big one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the contents, could you say when this conversation took place and what was actually happening on the ground at that time?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the middle of the war in 1991. The month was July, before the beginning of August, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was happening at that time on the ground involving Uzelac, Knin, Krajina? Can you explain what the two men are talking about?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About collecting people together to form the Banja Luka Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that? What did you observe yourself at that time?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was present at a meeting between Karadzic and Uzelac.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we go into private session briefly? 10 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a meeting was that? Where did you meet? Who did you meet, and what was discussed?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in July 1991. I can't remember the exact day. Karadzic asked me to come to Banja Luka, to the Bosna Hotel, which is where a large group of people had already gathered. They were activists from the SDS from Bosanska Krajina. And from there we went on to -- I don't know if it was the command of the Banja Luka Corps or what. I think it was the headquarters, the command of the Banja Luka Corps - a new building at any rate - to attend a meeting with Nikola Uzelac, Uzelac, head of staff of the Banja Luka Corps. And this was a socio-political meeting, if I can call it that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that meeting, was the mobilisation of people into the Banja Luka Corps discussed?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Support for the corps was discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that actually -- was it -- were you successful recruiting people for the Banja Luka Corps?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this was done on the territory of Bosanska Krajina, and the process was an ongoing one. First of all, with volunteers. So people started off by going on a voluntary basis, as volunteers, and then later on there were reinforcements. This is what people from the area told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Milosevic makes a reference in this conversation that we heard to the future RAM. Do you know what that is? What is RAM?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't heard of RAM.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go into open session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next tab, the intercept is number 40, and it is -- I do not intend to have that played, just I have highlighted a few sections, and the first highlighted section is on page 7 of the English, and it's actually on the bottom of the page and also on the -- it goes over into the following page on top. Can we have it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, it's actually the first marked part in your Serbian script. Mr. Karadzic says: RADOVAN KARADZIC: Uh-huh, this Minister over here and the deputy of ours were at the General Staff. Some kind of agreement was made for the police ... for MUP and army to maintain the order down there in the Neretva valley. And reserves should be situated in Bileca and in Trebinje at the barracks. I think that's not a bad idea? And Mr. Milosevic: SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Well, it's not, especially for Trebinje and Bileca as well. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yeah, it's all close to Neretva, and people will be safer. They will be at the barracks. That's a different thing, you know. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: That is OK, but up there is very important. Krajina, that's very important. Witness, first of all, did you listen to this conversation during your talks with the Prosecutor here in The Hague, and, if so, did you recognise who was speaking?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I listened to it. It was a conversation between Karadzic and Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what I just quoted to you, what -- what is the -- what is the background of this conversation about Bileca, Trebinje, the Neretva valley, and Krajina?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of mobilisation and putting up the reservists from Serbia in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit more precise? What was going on at that time? And can you tell us, first of all, at what time did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September 1991. That's when the conversation probably took place, which was the period when there was a mass mobilisation in Serbia, and the reservists who had been mobilised, the units, were sent towards Krajina via Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Neretva valley, is that an important strategic valley for -- in relation to the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Not in relation to Krajina but in relation to Dubrovnik and a confrontation there. That is where Serbian and Croatian territories meet in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as Karadzic explained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can now go to the next highlighted section. And the reference for Your Honours, it's on page 10. It starts actually in the middle, in the middle of this page with Mr. Milosevic saying, "Be careful..." and it ends actually on the next page. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Be careful, can you secure the normal passage of units through Bosnia with this part, this one from Serbia? Towards, towards, for example, Krajina? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Towards Krajina? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yes. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Well, I think we will be able to do it. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Come, concentrate on this question, because the answer to this question is very important to me. RADOVAN KARADZIC: I think we will be able, I mean, on the Doboj line, and then there. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Well, check that, and then we will see. Because I see that these, these have problems, these people to, to... RADOVAN KARADZIC: To have them transferred? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: To have them transferred, even to have Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. medicine, food transferred. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: All that needs help there, those people there. RADOVAN KARADZIC: I think we can ensure that, there will be no problems. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Yes, that is... RADOVAN KARADZIC: Because we will secure one of the lines and I will notify, I mean. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Good, notify. But notify in a safe way. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, yes. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Right. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Good, just so we know in advance, so. Torbavica informed me yesterday night at 12.00 that he will be setting off at 04.00 and then I, we secure the first convoy, and then four got lost. Do you know about convoys through -- from Serbia through Bosnia to the Krajina? Do you know of such convoys?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were brigades, JNA brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where did they come and where did they go at that time?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigades were coming from, as far as I know, Vojvodina province, Sabac, Loznica, and other areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they going?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, some of those units were deployed in Banija and Kordun, Lika, and some of the others elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know about these matters?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an insight from the field, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is also a person mentioned, Torbavica. Do you know who that is? That was actually in the last part that I read. Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, it could have been General Torbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General of what units and what position? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A JNA General. I think he was commander of the Uzice Corps or, rather, some units which were in the region.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. We can now turn to the next tab, and it's also one I do not want to play. It's tab 15. And I have highlighted a few passages for the witness and to be put on the ELMO. And, Your Honours, it starts on page 3 of the English text, in the middle of the text after the references to Wijnaendts. After the references to Wijnaendts, Radovan Karadzic says: RADOVAN KARADZIC: OK, what can be done here? Could Jovica do something about this? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: No, he cannot do anything. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Because, there he has those other, he, he, there, there he has a strong opposition among those smarter people. SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: To tell you the truth, I don't know what to do ... what, what is worth talking with them and I don't -- in what capacity can I support them when they are refusing to participate in the talks anyway? RADOVAN KARADZIC: Yes, unbelievable. You know what would be good? It would be good if Jovica would invite ten or so, that ten or so, to go there, smart people. I could also come to the meeting, and some things could be determined. They cannot do so, can they? SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: Absolutely! RADOVAN KARADZIC: There can't be, there can't be an opposition to force him. Not the one to relieve him from the office, but to force him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Private session, please. 7 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, about whom are they talking? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was going on at that time? You have already spoken about international meetings. What were they criticising, and why were they talking even of "relieve him from his office"?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It started with the work of the conference on Yugoslavia in The Hague, and to attend the conference the republics, representatives of the republics, were invited to participate on a footing of equality. I was offered, myself, as a representative of the people in Krajina, to take part in the conference, in the subcommittee for minorities, and I insisted that we be, that is to say the representatives of Krajina, be equitable participants in the conference. And it was via Misa Milosevic in Geneva that we presented our views vis-a-vis the conference. We stated our positions. And Milosevic was opposed to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did -- did actually Jovica try to influence the situation in the Krajina? Did he try to contact you? Did he even try to dismiss you, or, rather, have you dismissed?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the Assembly organisation and a campaign saying that I was a traitor, and I've already spoken about that. With respect to a meeting at President Milosevic's office which was a preparatory meeting prior to our departure for The Hague and Paris.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I forgot to ask you, did you listen to the entire tape while you had your conversations with --

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the Prosecutor, and did you recognise the voices of Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did listen to the entire tape, and yes, I did recognise their voices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at around what time did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means it was conducted around the 8th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to turn now to tab 42, and it's also nothing to be played, and I have highlighted for the witness actually two parts. I'm just told that it's not highlighted, but it's easy to find. For Your Honours, on the first page, on the first page, on the bottom, the last few sentences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, it should also be on your first page. There is a reference, when you put the first page on the ELMO, the translation, yes. Mr. Milosevic -- first of all, I have to ask you. Did you listen to this tape and did you recognise the voices?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I quote first from the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it seems so. You know, he wants complete serenity and independence like Macedonia, fuck it. And Radovan says. RADOVAN KARADZIC: Well, that's unbelievable. How will those people over there answer him? There's a large meeting of Montenegrins at the Sava Centre tomorrow. Witness, seeing this quote, what -- what kind of a meeting was at the Sava Centre? Do you know that, and who wanted complete sovereignty they are talking about here?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about criticism of Momir Bulatovic and the campaign which Milosevic launched against him for him to change his position with respect to The Hague conference and the acceptance of Carrington's plan for Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that Mr. Milosevic launched a campaign to change Mr. Bulatovic's position? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard this personally from Milosevic. I heard this personally from Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the occasion that you already talked about when he was complaining about Mr. Bulatovic?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. On the 20th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he actually say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that what must be borne in mind is that something that is not contained in these conversations cannot be interpreted. If the names that the witness is mentioning are not in here, he cannot mention them. He cannot interpret them in the context of what it says here. I think that would be right. He recognised the voices, but he cannot interpret something about which we do have enough information here. Especially, he should not mention names that do not exist in this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He says they do. I wonder really whether it takes us very much further. We have heard evidence about this. Do you want to refer to any other passages?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And actually, the witness had mentioned in relation to the Sava Centre a Montenegrin gathering. He concluded that the person talked about is -- but, yes, I would like to -- just one more quote here, and it's -- in the English text it's page 5, and it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we've heard it already, page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I have it marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I wasn't aware that I had already discussed this one. Thank you very much. The next tab -- the next one is tab 44, and it's also not to be played. I just would like to have the witness have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the first page, Mr. Milosevic -- first of all, did you listen to this tape during your conversation, and did you recognise the voices?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I recognised the voices of Karadzic and Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We -- on the first page there is marked -- there are marked actually three different parts: SLOBODAN MILOSEVIC: The maps were shown to me yesterday. The whole Eastern Slavonia was placed on them; Western Slavonia was partly presented on them, just like an island that will be authorised by UN. After that Krajina without Knin, without Knin, without Obrovac, Benkovac, Donji Lapac... Seeing this quote, do you know at what time this conversation took place and to which maps Mr. Milosevic is referring to? What maps were discussed at that time?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The discussion was on the 21st of November, 1991, and then it went on. It was the end of November. And this was regarding the maps of the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And I think the rest of the text speaks for itself, and we would not need to discuss it. The highlighted parts also speak for themselves. The witness has already described what was discussed with whom at that time. The next tab is 45.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you listen in to this tape?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And we have to go into private session for this one. 3 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually hear several tapes during which Radovan Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic criticise your position in relation to the international negotiations, be it the Carrington Plan or the Vance Plan, and is this one of them?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this conversation is one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I don't think we need to discuss it any further, because the witness has described the matter already enough. And this needs to be under seal, Your Honour. The last intercept in this context is tab 50, and I have actually marked two parts of it. The first part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff. The reason the tab 45 should be under seal is that -- because there's mention of this witness. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then how about tab 44? Some previous passage you read, there's also mention of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think now that I consider it, we do not need to have this under seal because nobody would know -- could detect from the document as such who the witness is. So nobody could detect anything. So we wouldn't need -- we wouldn't need to redact any names or have all these things where names are mentioned under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And tab 50, I have marked one passage on page 5 in the English version, and in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have to be in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we don't.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, tab 50, the first marked section. First of all, did you listen in to this conversation?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you recognise the voices?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Karadzic and Dobrica Cosic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On -- in this marked passage, Mr. Karadzic refers to ecological data and cartographers "...have produced the fairest variant in which we have sixty-one point three per cent of the land." And then they discuss these figures further. Did Mr. Karadzic make those kind of arguments when discussing about the land that should be under Serb control? Did he make these kind of arguments?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about talks with the representatives of Franjo Tudjman and the Croatian government, that is to say between them and Karadzic and the representatives of the authorities of Republika Srpska. I also know of a conversation I already mentioned at Slobodan Milosevic's in this context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And the next passage I have marked is on page 12. It's the top of page 12. Mr. Cosic and Mr. Karadzic speak about a removal of a person, and they speak about tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have to go into private session for this. 6 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this passage, are they speaking about your removal from your position?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when this conversation -- can you place it in time? Because it says here: "DC: Yes, if they remove him tomorrow that will mean something..." Do you know when this conversation took place from this context?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A day before the 16th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That should be enough, and we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next series of intercepts I do not want to discuss or play with the witness in detail. I just want to ask him some general questions about intercepts that he heard in a certain context and only speak about a very few voices that are heard on these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. intercepts and how he is familiar with these voices, because he had actually made this declaration reference to all of these intercepts and explained in this declaration whom he recognised, and I would just find out in relation to several of those intercepts mentioned in the declaration how he knows the voices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that would be a suitable matter to deal with after the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're on page 64, I take it, paragraph 319; is that right? You can tell us afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put to the witness only briefly the transcripts of the intercepted conversations 23, 25, and tab 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first one is an intercepted conversation between Karadzic and Grahovac of the 24th of June, 1991, Witness. And the second one is a conversation between Karadzic and Vukic from that same day, and the third one is a conversation between Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic of the 9th of July, 1991. Did you have opportunity to listen in to these three conversations?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 2? I have under tab 2 a conversation with Karadzic; tab 3, Karadzic, Cosic. I don't know what the point is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with tab 2, Karadzic and Cosic. Tab 23. Was that the next one you had, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had tab 23, tab 25, and tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. And tab 2 is an intercept between Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic, dated the 9th of July, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I have that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The voice of -- how familiar are you with the voice of Mr. Grahovac? Do you know his voice and how?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We talked often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this other person, Vukic, would you know who that is? The conversation Karadzic, Vukic.

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Vukic from Banja Luka, president of the Municipal Board of the SDS in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with his voice?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I'm not sure about his voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Private session for one question, Your Honour. 3 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In these three conversations that these people had, did they criticise you for your step in relation to the unification of the two Krajinas? Is that part of these three conversations?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not everybody criticised me. Milosevic and Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But the contents -- the contents of these three conversations, do they refer to your actions in relation to the unification of the Krajinas?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go back into open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other day, you also mentioned that despite the criticism against the unification of the two Krajinas, later on the -- Mr. Karadzic himself pursued that same aim, and in relation to that, I would like to put to the witness the exhibit -- tab 107 of Exhibit 352, and it's just for you to have a look at it and whether you can authenticate this document. It's the "Prijedor declaration on the Unification of the RSK and the RS," of the 31st of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And I would like to move now on with the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And for your orientation, Your Honour, the three intercepts we just mentioned in relation to the unification and this issue was paragraph 163 of the proofing summary, and we are now back on 319, where a lot of intercepts are actually listed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the intercepts listed under this paragraph, I would like to put to the witness just briefly the intercepts tab 4 and tab 5. Witness, these two intercepts are of -- are of unclear date. It's not given. But in both of these intercepts, reference is made to a referendum in Bosnia. Can you tell us from their contents on what -- at what time these conversations may have taken place giving these contents?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning of November. The end of October -- no. November more probably, 1991, after the referendum was held when part of the MPs of the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, those who were of Serb ethnicity, and the SDS, when they conducted this referendum in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I do not want to put the other exhibits to the witness except for these -- where I mentioned we haven't yet spoken about the names -- the voices of these people. Did you listen in to an intercept between Karadzic and Vucurevic? And that would be tab 32.

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you -- how are you familiar, if at all, with the voice of Mr. Vucurevic?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although I met him only once or two or three times, but I listened to his speeches. He has such a characteristic voice that one has to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is characteristic about the voice of Mr. Vucurevic?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the intonation, the depth, the mode of speech, the accent a very special type of voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of an accent does he have?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Herzegovinian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have also intercepts with the voice of -- it's actually tab 41 is an intercept between Karadzic and Jovic, and I would like to know from you how familiar you are with the voice of Mr. Jovic and whether you are able to recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know it well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From many personal contacts and meetings I had with him, I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have also one intercept. It's tab 46. One intercept between Mr. Karadzic and Mrs. Plavsic, Biljana Plavsic. Did you listen into this intercept as well, and did you recognise the voices?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I recognised both the voices of Karadzic and Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How familiar are you with Mrs. Plavsic's voice? How do you know it?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have frequently had meetings with her in person.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not think that I have to put now all the other intercepts with Karadzic in front of the witness. I think they should be accepted in the form of the declaration, because I would not need to discuss the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the matter is still, of course, for the Chamber to decide whether they'll be admitted or not. They have been marked for identification, but of course, there is no need for this witness to go through them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. I will now continue with paragraph 320 in the proofing summary and turn to the military formations on the ground in the SAO Krajina, in particular in the regions where crimes were committed according to the indictment against Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The northern part of the SAO Krajina, in particular the region of Kostajnica and Korenica, did they belong to the 5th Military District of the JNA with headquarters in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the 5th Military District?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think it was General Raseta. He was either the commander or deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which JNA corps covered these regions?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zagreb Corps and the Rijeka Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Rijeka Corps, did they also -- did they also belong to the 5th Military District?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did. They were between the Military Naval District and the 5th Military District. I'm not sure, though, whether they were the 5th District or the Military Naval District.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this region of -- in this region that I just mentioned, Kostajnica and Korenica, were there any military barracks, and if so, where were they and --

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of the JNA barracks in Petrinja, the JNA barracks in Karlovac, the military training ground for the artillery close to Slunj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of this artillery training ground in Slunj? During the events, that is, summer of 1991, autumn 1991.

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of Colonel Cedomir Bulat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How -- what is -- how do you know him and his position?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I was told by the President of the municipality of Slunj at the end of November 1991 that Colonel Cedomir Bulat had taken control of Slunj, which until then had been under the control of the forces of the Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulat, was he a JNA officer, and if so, what rank did he have?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. He was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And who was the commander in Petrinja?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a time it was Slobodan Tarbuk, a colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which time was he the commander?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of the fighting in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The southern part of the SAO with Knin, Benkovac, was it part of the JNA coastal district with headquarters in Split?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the -- this coastal district?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Admiral Mile Kandic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which corps covered this region? Which JNA corps?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th Corps of the JNA, the Knin Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned General Vukovic being the commander. From what time onwards was he the commander?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime around the mid of September 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the Knin Corps commander received his orders? Did he receive it through Split, or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Vukovic received orders from the General Staff in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? And if necessary, we can go into private session. Private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Private session, Your Honour. 14 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are in private session. How do you know that Mr. Vukovic got his orders directly from the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From at least three pieces of information. The first was that he took over duty under summary procedure from the then federal secretary, General Veljko Kadijevic, and that is how he came to Knin. The second point is something that he told me personally, as he did the first point, that he had received orders to move the forces of the corps at the beginning of October 1991. And third: Around the 10th of October, he named the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army as his Superior Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Knin Corps also report directly to Belgrade about all actions? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had occasion to listen to a conversation between General Adzic and Colonel Ratko Mladic at the beginning of September 1991. Mladic played the tape of this conversation for me, when Adzic criticised him why they had captured the Maslenica bridge without having received prior orders to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the circumstances? What was the topic that you discussed that made him play the tape to you? What was the particular reason for him to do so?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was the following: In those days, the commander of the Knin Corps was General Spiro Nikolic, and Colonel Mladic and some other officers from the corps, without General Spiro Nikolic knowing about it, carried out the capture of the Maslenica bridge. General Adzic punished Spiro Nikolic for this and replaced him from that position as a result, and he criticised Mladic for doing this. And then Mladic wanted to show me and play this conversation for me, and he asked me whether I knew, through political channels, anything more about this position in Belgrade. And I said that I did not, and that was how the conversation ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Kasum say anything to you about the independence or the dependence and the actions, the orders from Belgrade to the Knin Corps?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in October 1991. He was commenting on a particular event - I can't remember which one - and he said the following: that in the General Staff in Belgrade, there was an operations map and that not a single tank on the ground can move without the permission of the General Staff in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go back into open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, it would be, in my opinion, very helpful if you put into a form of a chart what this witness had said in relation to the military formation of JNA, or something like that. And you may name it as a chain of command or formation of military thing. Before -- and have this witness confirm before he leaves here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we can do that, but I'm not sure that we can really manage it until Monday. We will try our best to do that, but would it also be possible to do that in re-direct? Would you allow for that, if re-direct is necessary? Because it's a rather complex matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, whatever will be convenient for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we have already discussed the formation of the TO and the problems that existed there. In relation to the formations on the ground, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I would like to put to you just a few additional documents that we have so far not addressed. The first one is tab 112 of binder 352, in relation to the TO and the RSK, the RSK army. And I have here a military document from the Supreme Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia Personnel Department of the 29th of April, 1994, to the Forward Section of the RSK, in relation to temporary assignment of work of civil persons. And I would -- I would like to know from you: Where was the Forward Section of the RSK army? Do you know where it was situated?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the representative offices of the RSK in Belgrade. That was the Advance Department of the Ministry of Defence of RSK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at the document and the person signing this document, the stamps and the header, is this -- can you say anything about the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the letterhead and the stamp, I can say that it is authentic, and that is confirmed by the next document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So another document goes with it, and that's actually, Your Honour, tab 113.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Sorry. Yes. There is a second page to it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this second page confirm?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It confirms the authenticity of the document we are discussing, its content and the signatories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you actually provide these two documents to the Prosecution during your conversations here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person, Major General Dusan Zoric, who was he?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Head of the personnel administration of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document, is there actually a transfer facilitated from a person from the RSK army to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which person, please?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document under number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's Dijana Kovacevic? Is that the person had who was actually working for the RSK and was then transferred to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the authorities of the RSK army, were they actually asked when such transfers were facilitated, or did they just have to accept it?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They accepted it, or they agreed with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question: Were they asked in advance? When such transfers were ordered, were the authorities in RSK army, were they asked?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This went according to order, and the person was informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And with the help of the usher, I would put to the witness now tab 113, or has he already -- he has it already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is now a document from the 18th Corps Command of the 17th of March, 1994, regulating the status of military recruits, and it is signed by commander Colonel Lazo Babic, and it is a stamp from the military post Okucane. This document, is it -- looking at the header, the stamp, and the signature, is that a authentic document?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't have a signature, but there's the name written, and an authentic stamp and heading. And that person, as such, existed over there with that position, in that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want to say something, Mr. Milosevic? If so, we can't hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was saying that tab 11, but which binder? It's not in this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No. It's actually 113.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Sorry. 113, yes. We've dealt with 111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment while the accused finds it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this document relates to the -- actually, the status of military recruits, and from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Were they recruits from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia doing their service in the army of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a practice, that recruits from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia did their service in the RSK, and was that also the practice the other way around?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the other way around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From -- in which time periods was this a practice?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the period of existence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was this organised?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the competent administrations of the Army of Yugoslavia and the Army of the Republic of Srpska Krajina, that is, through the administration of the army of Yugoslavia that was in charge of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Another exhibit I would like to put to the witness is tab 152 from that same binder of exhibits, 352, and it's an order by Colonel General Zivota Panic. I have French translation now. It's obviously not my ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at the header and the stamp on the document, and also the signature, can you comment on the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an authentic document, but I don't recognise the signature of Zivota Panic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in the position given in the document, that is, Chief of Staff of the Yugoslav army at that time, that is, in -- on the 27th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that document also referring to the practice of acceptance and initiating of conscript soldiers into the army of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, sir, you mentioned that the RSK army was not an independent army, and you mentioned also that Mr. Milosevic appointed its leading officers. In relation to this remark of yours, did you mean that he officially appointed the leading officers, or in which way did he deal with the appointment of officers?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He decided de facto, but officially it was implemented by the competent bodies, such as the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, or the Presidency, while the SFRY was in existence, or rather, the Supreme Council of Defence when it became the FRY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to materiel supplies, I would like to put to you the Exhibits 153 -- tab 153, Exhibit 352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before you go on, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, may I ask the witness whether he has examples of officers so appointed by Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mile Mrksic, for instance, the last commander. I'm sorry. I haven't said everything. Officially, this was implemented also by the bodies of the Republic of Srpska Krajina and the competent bodies of the Army of Yugoslavia. One example of that is General Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What you mean, then, is that he made the appointment and it was officially confirmed by the proper authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He really decided, and de facto decided, who would be the commander, and the authorities would confirm that through documents, procedurally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How would you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I participated in the formal and legal decision-making of Milosevic's practical decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had actually discussed this situation, and several other situations of that kind, when we went through the meetings that took place with Mr. Milosevic, and he -- the witness gave some examples where those matters were discussed and decided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to materiel supplies, I would like to put to you the document tab 153. It's a request of the Ministry of Defence of the RSK, of the 8th of April 1993, to the Chief of General Staff of the VJ, for Orkan rockets and other rockets, and it is signed by Deputy Minister Lieutenant Colonel Dusko Babic. And I would like you -- I would like you to comment on the authenticity in relation to the header, the stamp, and the signature.

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's authentic, only I can't recognise the signature. Everything else is authentic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the RSK army receive Orkan rockets, for instance, Orkan rockets, or the unguided rockets, from the VJ? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you get knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Orkan from people who manned Orkan or had connections with it, and I also heard of these other rockets.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like now to put to the witness the Exhibit 157, and it's -- sorry, the tab 157 from that same exhibit, and it refers to an order by Commander Colonel Milan Celeketic, of the 23rd of December, 1993, in relation to how materials should be received and requested from the VJ. And it says here: "Requests to the VJ for MS replenishment of the units are to be sent directly to the Corps Command. I strictly forbid subordinate commands and individuals to directly contact the General Staff of the VJ or the VJ units in order to secure MS."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
