utterances.text: Was there a practice at that time, in December 1993, that units would send their request directly to the VJ, and is that a reason for this order? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that the situation in the Army of the Republic of Srpska Krajina was chaotic at the time, and this is the result of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like now to put to the witness the tab 155 of that same exhibit. It is a request for materiel to form a military naval fleet, of the 19th of September. And the year is actually left open, but in the document as such, it is a meeting -- is referred to a meeting held on the 9th of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, in relation to authenticity, do you recognise the header, the stamp, and the signature of General Celeketic?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the heading and stamp. Celeketic was indeed the commander at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know anything about a meeting held on the 9th of September, 1994 in relation to a river force? Are you aware of this meeting that is mentioned here in this document?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether such a river -- military naval fleet was then actually founded and equipped?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next document is tab 156. It's a letter from the RSK Cabinet of the President to the President of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this -- looking at the header, the stamp, and the signature, is this Goran Hadzic's signature? Is that the stamp used at that time and the head of the letter?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the stamp. And the signature resembles it. I'm not quite sure whether it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic in this letter is asking for military personnel, especially for junior officers, performing duties of commanders and commandants, and also for military judges and prosecutors. Are you aware that this was actually requested at that time?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the request, but I do know that at that time, or after that time, people did come in, officers did come in, to set up military courts and prosecutors' offices. A man did come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, tab 159. It's a report of the RSK Ministry of Defence, dated the 7th of February, 1995, in relation to materiel, technical support, from the FRY and the Serbian Republic. Do you know this report, and can you say anything about its authenticity, looking at the format of this report and the header, stamp, and signature?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no stamp on signature, but it's a report that I know about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Who made this report?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of Defence of the RSK, Colonel Rade Tanjga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it refers to specific means that were obtained. And the figures in this report, do they correspond with your memory of matters?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. A thousand tonnes. Well, I can't quite remember now exactly what the quantity was. According to this, that's the figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next document is tab 122. It's an order to form the headquarters and units of the Territorial Defence of the municipalities of the SAO Krajina, from the 21st of August, 1991. Do you remember that this decision was made at that time?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next is tab 116. It's an order establishing -- establishments of Territorial Defence staff and units of the SAO Krajina, from the 21st of August, 1991. Was such a decision made?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same document. Yes. This is an identical document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Sorry. Thank you. Thank you for this advice. Tab 120, then, please. It's a document in relation to the creation of operative zones. And the 1st Operative Zone is Dalmatinsko-Licka, with the municipalities of Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, Donji Lapac and Korenica. The 2nd Operative Zone is Kordun, with Slunj in it. And the 3rd Operative Zone is Dvor na Uni, Glina, Kostajnica, Petrinja and Sisak. Do you recall who were the commanders in these three zones? Do you know? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian commander should have been the prime minister of the government of SAO Krajina. At the end of September, the Main Staff of the Territorial Defence of SAO Krajina was set up, and it began functioning at the beginning of October. The commander was General Ilija Djujic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. This we have already discussed. I was asking you for the commanders of the 1st Operative Zone, the level below the, head. The level below the Main Staff. Do you know who was the commander in the region of the 1st Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were municipal staffs of Territorial Defence and units subordinate to the municipal staffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And between the Main Staff and those municipal staffs, was there another layer of command? Was there a 1st Operative Zone commander or 2nd Operative Zone commander and 3rd Operative Zone Commander?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it should have been the commander of the Main Staff of the TO of SAO Krajina, and the 2nd and 3rd zones were changeable, variable. At the end, it was Colonel Vujaklija who was commander of the 2nd and 3rd, a JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this context there is yet another document, tab 127 of that same exhibit, and it relates, actually, to the Unified Territorial Defence Staff is formed for the 2nd and 3rd Operative Zone. And that is this person that you just mentioned, Vujaklija, then?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order on the unification of the zones into one zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and my question was: Was Mr. Vujaklija the commander of this combined zone?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another document, tab 133. It's also in relation to the structure of the TO of the region Gracac, Donji Lapac, and Korenica, of the 5th of October, 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about a few specific corps or divisions that were in the regions of -- the region of Kostajnica, Petrinja, and Korenica. Was there a 7th Banija Division; and if so, what kind of unit was it and where did it operate?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 7th Banija Division, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it operating, and what kind of a division was it? I mean, was it TO or was it JNA?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a volunteer unit organised by the parallel structures which functioned in the Dvor na Uni, Kostajnica municipalities, and parts of Glina, Petrinja, and later on exclusively in the area of Dvor na Uni and Kostajnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was its commander in autumn 1991?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogdan Vajagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom was he subordinated?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the end of September 1991, the parallel structures had the command over him, and he was subordinated with the Petrinja garrison of the JNA. As of October, or rather, when the command was set up of the JNA Operative Group for Kordun and Banija, he was subordinated to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said "parallel structure," do you mean this Martic, Frenki group?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: DB Serbia: Martic, Frenki, and the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the 6th Lika Division? Can you explain what kind of a unit that was and to which it was subordinated?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a JNA unit. In a sense, it was a volunteer unit, but nonetheless it was a JNA unit. And it was commanded by Savo Jurasovic, a colonel, who was a commanding officer in Gospic before that, a JNA officer. I don't know for how long.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness Exhibit 128. That's an order regarding the appointment of Djuro Vujaklija, commander of the TO forces of the 2nd and 3rd Operative Zone, from the 30th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The headquarters of Mr. Vujaklija, where were they?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vojnic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom did he report?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Operative Group of the JNA, Jasan Maric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the headquarters of this operative group?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Samarica Hill, which means are the Kostajnica, Dvor, and Petrinja municipalities meet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And this 6th Lika Division that we just spoke about a moment earlier, was that in -- was that related to that same headquarters in Samarica, or where did it operate?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It operated in the Lika area. It had its headquarters by the Plitvice Lakes, at Mukinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have already mentioned at an earlier stage of your testimony the pattern of conduct that occurred, and you said already that you saw it happen in the Kostajnica region with -- and in Dubica, Cerovljani, and Bacin. Are they located in this region? And do you know when those villages were attacked and who actually attacked them? Which corps and which TO units?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting was started by the 7th Banija Volunteer Division, in the area of Dvor and Kostajnica. Later on, the Petrinja garrison of the JNA joined in. And later on these units -- the 7th Banija accepted being a TO unit but didn't place itself under the competent commands of the TO, up until the formation of the command of the operative group at Samarica, when it was subordinated. Then, in that same area, we saw the involvement of the Loznica Brigade, from Serbia. It was mobilised in the region of Sunj, towards Kostajnica. I don't know what the deployment of that unit was exactly. And the special police units forces of Krajina were active there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, who was the overall commander during the attack on the villages Dubica, Cerovljani, and Bacin? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when the attacks on these villages took place. The fighting around Kostajnica took place until the end of September. That means the 7th Banija and the Petrinja garrison of the JNA joined forces there up until that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned that you -- that these villages were destroyed in a certain pattern. Did that happen during that fighting that you just mentioned, end of September, or at a later date?

utterances.speaker: M. BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed through those villages in November, or near the villages, at least, in mid-November 1991. And they had been destroyed after that fighting, that is to say, in those battles, up to the time when I passed by and saw them, before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, when it's a convenient moment. We seem to be going on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are actually in the crime scenes. We are now actually already in the crime scenes, paragraph 337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be convenient to adjourn now and go on on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.
